title: Vulnerability Management: Scanner Synthesis & Remediation Tracker (Q1 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This document synthesizes vulnerability scanner outputs from our Q1 2026 automated runs, defines patch SLAs, and tracks remediation for high / critical findings across hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments. It also contains brief dependency review notes and recommended automation for evidence collection and SIEM export mapping.

Scope & cadence:
- Scans included: Trivy (container/image), Snyk (dependencies), Dependabot (repo PRs), Nessus (infrastructure surface), and internal static results from 'sast-lite' (quick CI SAST).
- Date range: 2026-01-01 -> 2026-02-28 (two full monthly runs + ad-hoc infra scan).
- Coverage: production clusters (region-us-east-1, eu-west-1), internal CI runners, and public-facing load balancers.

High-level totals (combined):
- Total unique findings: 428
- Critical (CVSS >= 9.0): 12
- High (7.0 <= CVSS < 9.0): 58
- Medium: 210
- Low/Informational: 148
- False positives / already mitigated: 34 (flagged and suppressed)

Top critical findings (representative snippets):
1) CVE-2024-42829 (critical) - affected: openjdk:17-jdk image used by batch-worker service
   - Scanner: Trivy 0.41.0 (image scan on: runtime/batch-worker:20260201)
   - Evidence: "Package: openjdk; Installed: 17.0.8; CVE: CVE-2024-42829; Description: Deserialization RCE in ...; Fix: upgrade-openjdk-17.0.9+..."
   - Risk: remote code execution in workloads that accept serialized input (batch-worker processes user uploads)
   - Action: patch base image & rebuild container; backport minimal mitigation for input validation in worker.

2) CVE-2025-1177 (critical) - affected: nginx 1.20.x in edge-router config (eu-west-1)
   - Scanner: Nessus 10.4
   - Evidence: "libnginx malformed header parsing leads to memory corruption..."
   - Action: upgrade to 1.22.x or apply vendor patch; schedule emergency deploy to EU region only.

3) CVE-2024-xxxxx (supply-chain critical) - malicious package flagged by Snyk in a transitive dependency of telemetry-agent
   - Scanner: Snyk / dependency tree analysis
   - Evidence: signature mismatch in tarball, provenance mismatch
   - Action: temporary removal of telemetry-agent from starter images; dependency maintainers notified; mitigation: pin to audited fork.

Patch SLA (policy proposal):
- Critical (exploitable, CVSS >= 9.0 OR active exploit): 72 hours to patch + deploy to affected environments; emergency rollback plan if deployment fails.
- High (7.0-8.9): 14 calendar days to patch and verify in staging; deploy in next release window unless compensating control exists.
- Medium (4.0-6.9): 60 calendar days to remediate or accept with documented risk, periodic review every 30 days.
- Low (<4.0): 120 days, schedule into normal maintenance cycles.
- Exceptions: documented in JIRA with risk acceptance by head of security and product owner.

Remediation tracker (selected items):
- RID-001: openjdk base image - CVE-2024-42829
  - Owner: runtime-team (Jared Kim)
  - Status: in_progress
  - Action: bump base image to 17.0.9, rebuild images, run smoke tests (CI-2457)
  - ETA: 2026-02-05 (missed, now target 2026-02-12)
  - Notes: need approval for updated image from QA due to JNI changes.

- RID-002: nginx edge-router - CVE-2025-1177
  - Owner: infra-network (Liam Chen)
  - Status: scheduled
  - Action: apply vendor hotfix; canary deploy to eu-west-1 first
  - ETA: 2026-02-04 (canary), full roll 2026-02-06
  - Notes: coordinate with Dedicated customers in EU; notify support.

- RID-003: telemetry-agent dep issue (supply-chain)
  - Owner: devexp (Marisol Rivera)
  - Status: mitigated (temporary removal)
  - Action: pin to audited fork; open PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/433
  - ETA: 2026-02-20

Remediation statuses (summary):
- Critical: 12 total -> 7 closed, 4 in_progress, 1 accepted with mitigation
- High: 58 total -> 22 closed, 30 in_progress, 6 deferred with compensating controls

False positive handling and evidence automation notes:
- We observed noise from Snyk on dev-only test packages and a redundant CI image. Proposed automation: add a CI-flagged metadata label (e.g., rw:ci_env=true) to exclude certain images from production scans; automated suppression rule creation requires one human reviewer.
- Evidence collection: standardize 'scan-run' artifacts (JSON) to include fields: scanner_name, scanner_version, scan_time, target_type, target_id, finding_id, cve_ids (array), severity, risk_vector, reproducible_command, remediation_reference, proof_blob_url.
- Action item: implement lightweight evidence bundler (Lambda) that consumes scanner webhooks and stores canonical JSON in encrypted object storage with S3 path encoded: s3://redwood-security-scans/<env>/<scanner>/<yyyy-mm-dd>/<target>-<scanid>.json

Dependency review notes (manual reviews performed during Feb):
- runtime/container-helpers: moved from lodash-es 4.x to 5.x; review found no suspicious API changes. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/container-helpers/pull/122
- console/frontend: flagged a devDependency (left-pad-sim) due to typosquatting indicators; team replaced with internal shim and added package-sig verification in CI.
- Private deployment package: added SBOM generation step (CycloneDX) to build pipeline to aid auditors.

SIEM export mapping (recommended minimal schema):
- event_type: "vuln.scan.finding"
- timestamp: scan_time (ISO8601)
- source: scanner_name
- scanner_version: scanner_version
- env: production|staging|dev
- target: target_id (image:tag or host)
- finding_id: finding_id
- cve: cve_ids (pipe-separated if multiple)
- severity: severity (critical/high/medium/low)
- cvss: cvss_score
- status: open|in_progress|fixed|accepted
- owner: owner_team
- remediation_ref: JIRA key or PR URL
- evidence_url: S3 URL to canonical scan JSON

Notes on SIEM export and alerting:
- Critical findings should raise high-priority SIEM alert with automatic pager duty notification (integration: PD escalation rule VULN_CRIT_01).
- Enrich SIEM events with tagging: customer-impacting=true/false; deployment-mode=hosted|dedicated|private.

Manual verification checklist (for owners):
1) Confirm vulnerability exists in production artifact (not only in local dev image).
2) Reproduce minimal PoC or validate vendor advisory.
3) Create remediation PR with link to JIRA ticket and include test plan.
4) Run smoke and integration tests; perform canary if infra-impacting.
5) Update tracker entry and evidence JSON; mark as fixed in scanner and close when cleared by next full scan.

Risk acceptance and retrospective notes:
- One critical finding (RID-009) was accepted temporarily due to high risk of downtime; compensating control was WAF rule added and increased telemetry. Acceptance documented in JIRA-SEC-4377 with signed approval by Head of Product and Security.
- Retrospective: two processes need improvement: faster image rebuild pipeline (bottleneck: QA verification) and clearer on-call handoff for infra hotfixes.

Recommendations & next steps (prioritized):
- Short term (<= 30 days): implement evidence bundler webhook; hook Trivy & Snyk outputs into the SIEM schema; update incident runbooks for CVE-driven hotfixes.
- Medium term (30-90 days): enforce SBOM for all production images; enable image signing and verify in runtime admission controller; reduce rebuild QA friction by adding an automated smoke-worker test for JNI-sensitive images.
- Long term (90+ days): integrate dependency provenance checks (in-toto) in release pipeline; automate PD alerts for critical CVE events based on SIEM streams.

Appendix A: commands & quick reproductions (for infra/dev teams):
- Trivy image scan (example): trivy image --format json --output trivy-runtime-batch-20260201.json runtime/batch-worker:20260201
- Snyk test (node): snyk test --json > snyk-console-frontend-20260202.json
- Nessus export: use API v2 to pull scan id and export to CSV/nessus format; then run internal parser to map to canonical schema.

Appendix B: quick link checklist:
- Jira epic for Q1 remediation: JIRA-SEC-4321
- Evidence storage bucket: s3://redwood-security-scans/
- Canonical SIEM schema doc (draft): CONFLUENCE-1582

If you are owner of an open RID above, update the tracker with the latest PR/ETA and mark scanning evidence URL in the JIRA ticket. For questions or blockers, ping #security-ops and tag the on-call SRE.

-- Asha
